questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A pure semiconductor material, containing no deliberately added impurities, is called an
questions.explanation: An intrinsic semiconductor is in its pure form, without deliberately introduced impurities that would alter its conductive properties.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A semiconductor material that has been deliberately doped with impurities to alter its electrical properties is called an
questions.explanation: Extrinsic semiconductors are intentionally doped with impurity atoms to modify their conductivity, forming either P-type or N-type material.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The process of intentionally adding impurity atoms to a pure semiconductor to modify its electrical properties is called
questions.explanation: Doping introduces controlled amounts of impurity atoms into a semiconductor crystal, creating either P-type or N-type material.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: Semiconductor material doped with trivalent impurity atoms, such as boron, creating an excess of 'holes' (positive charge carriers), is called
questions.explanation: P-type semiconductor material is created by doping with trivalent atoms (like boron), producing an excess of positive charge carriers called holes.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: Semiconductor material doped with pentavalent impurity atoms, such as phosphorus, creating an excess of free electrons, is called
questions.explanation: N-type semiconductor material is created by doping with pentavalent atoms (like phosphorus), producing an excess of free electrons as charge carriers.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The junction formed where P-type and N-type semiconductor materials meet within a single crystal is called the
questions.explanation: The P-N junction is the boundary region where P-type and N-type materials meet, forming the basis of diodes and other semiconductor devices.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The narrow region around a P-N junction that becomes depleted of free charge carriers is called the
questions.explanation: The depletion layer is the region around the junction where charge carriers have diffused across and recombined, leaving it depleted of free carriers.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The small voltage that naturally develops across a P-N junction, opposing further diffusion of charge carriers, is called the
questions.explanation: The barrier potential is the built-in voltage across the depletion layer that must be overcome for significant current to flow through the junction.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: Applying a voltage to a P-N junction in a way that reduces the barrier potential and allows current to flow easily is called
questions.explanation: Forward biasing connects the voltage source so as to reduce the barrier potential, allowing current to flow readily through the junction.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: Applying a voltage to a P-N junction in a way that increases the barrier potential and prevents significant current flow is called
questions.explanation: Reverse biasing connects the voltage source so as to widen the depletion layer and increase the barrier, blocking significant current flow except a small leakage current.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A resistor manufactured from a mixture of carbon granules and a binding material, one of the most common and inexpensive types, is called a
questions.explanation: Carbon composition resistors are made from a compressed mixture of carbon and binder, offering a simple and inexpensive fixed resistance.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A resistor manufactured by depositing a thin resistive layer, such as carbon or metal, onto an insulating substrate, offering improved precision, is called a
questions.explanation: Film resistors deposit a thin resistive film onto a substrate, generally offering better precision and stability than carbon composition types.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A resistor manufactured by winding resistance wire around an insulating core, often used where higher power ratings are needed, is called a
questions.explanation: Wire-wound resistors use a coiled resistance wire, allowing them to handle higher power dissipation than typical carbon or film resistors.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A variable resistor with three terminals, commonly used to adjust voltage levels such as volume controls, is called a
questions.explanation: A potentiometer has three terminals and is typically used to create an adjustable voltage divider, such as in volume controls.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A variable resistor with two terminals, commonly used to control current in a circuit, is called a
questions.explanation: A rheostat typically uses two terminals to vary resistance and directly control current flow in a circuit.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The standardised system using coloured bands to indicate the resistance value and tolerance of a fixed resistor is called
questions.explanation: Resistor colour coding uses a standardised sequence of coloured bands to indicate a resistor's value, tolerance, and sometimes temperature coefficient.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A capacitor constructed using a polarised design, generally offering high capacitance in a compact size, is called an
questions.explanation: Electrolytic capacitors are polarised and can offer relatively high capacitance values in a compact package, but must be connected with correct polarity.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A capacitor constructed using a ceramic material as its dielectric, commonly small and non-polarised, is called a
questions.explanation: Ceramic capacitors use a ceramic dielectric and are typically small, non-polarised, and widely used for general-purpose applications.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The capacitance of a capacitor is defined by the formula
questions.explanation: Capacitance (C) is defined as the ratio of stored charge (Q) to the voltage (V) across the capacitor's plates.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: When capacitors are connected in parallel, the total capacitance is
options: the reciprocal of the sum of reciprocals of individual capacitances
the sum of all individual capacitances
always equal to the smallest individual capacitance
questions.explanation: Capacitors in parallel simply add their capacitance values together, unlike resistors in parallel.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: When capacitors are connected in series, the total capacitance is calculated using the
options: product of the individual capacitances directly
direct sum of the individual capacitances
questions.explanation: Series-connected capacitors combine using the reciprocal sum formula, analogous to how resistors combine in parallel.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A component made from a coil of wire, used to store energy in a magnetic field when current flows through it, is called an
questions.explanation: An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field generated by current flowing through its coiled winding.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: An inductor wound around a non-magnetic core, such as plastic or cardboard, is called an
questions.explanation: Air-core inductors are wound with no magnetic core material, typically used for lower-inductance, higher-frequency applications.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: An inductor wound around a magnetic material, such as laminated iron, generally providing a higher inductance for a given coil size, is called an
questions.explanation: Iron-core inductors use a magnetic core material to concentrate the magnetic field, achieving greater inductance than an equivalent air-core design.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The opposition an inductor presents to alternating current, which increases with frequency, is called its
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance (XL = 2*pi*f*L) increases with both frequency and inductance, representing the AC opposition presented by an inductor.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The opposition a capacitor presents to alternating current, which decreases as frequency increases, is called its
questions.explanation: Capacitive reactance decreases as frequency increases, the opposite behaviour to inductive reactance, reflecting how capacitors respond to AC signals.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A capacitor made using thin mica sheets as the dielectric material, valued for stability and precision at higher frequencies, is called a
questions.explanation: Mica capacitors use thin mica sheets as a dielectric, offering good stability and precision, often used in high-frequency and precision applications.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A capacitor whose capacitance value can be adjusted, commonly used for tuning circuits such as radio receivers, is called a
questions.explanation: Variable capacitors allow the capacitance value to be adjusted mechanically, commonly used for tuning applications such as radio receivers.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The first colour band on a resistor, read from the end closest to it, generally represents the
options: first significant digit of the resistance value
questions.explanation: The first colour band on a standard resistor indicates the first significant digit of its resistance value, following the standard colour code sequence.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The final colour band on many resistors, often gold or silver, typically indicates the
questions.explanation: The final band on a resistor typically indicates its tolerance, showing the permissible variation from its nominal stated value (e.g., gold for ±5%).

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: Energy stored in a charged capacitor is held in the form of an
questions.explanation: A capacitor stores energy in the electric field established between its two conductive plates, separated by the dielectric material.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: Energy stored in a current-carrying inductor is held in the form of a
options: electric current flowing indefinitely with no source
questions.explanation: An inductor stores energy in the magnetic field generated by current flowing through its coiled winding.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: Doping a semiconductor with a pentavalent element such as phosphorus adds extra electrons because phosphorus has
options: three valence electrons, one fewer than needed for the crystal lattice
five valence electrons, one more than needed for the four covalent bonds in the crystal lattice
exactly four valence electrons, matching silicon precisely
questions.explanation: Phosphorus has five valence electrons; four form covalent bonds within the silicon lattice, leaving one extra electron free to conduct.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: Doping a semiconductor with a trivalent element such as boron creates 'holes' because boron has
options: five valence electrons, one more than needed for the crystal lattice
three valence electrons, one fewer than needed to complete the four covalent bonds in the crystal lattice
exactly four valence electrons, matching silicon precisely
questions.explanation: Boron has only three valence electrons, leaving one covalent bond incomplete within the silicon lattice, creating a 'hole' that can accept an electron.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A basic semiconductor device that allows current to flow easily in one direction but blocks it in the other is called a
questions.explanation: A diode is a two-terminal semiconductor device that conducts current readily in one direction (forward biased) but blocks it in the reverse direction.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A diode primarily designed to handle small signal currents, commonly used in radio and communication circuits, is called a
questions.explanation: Signal diodes are optimised for handling small currents at typically higher frequencies, common in radio and communication circuit applications.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A diode designed to handle larger currents, commonly used to convert AC to DC in power supply circuits, is called a
questions.explanation: Power rectifier diodes are built to handle higher currents, making them suitable for converting AC to DC in power supply circuits.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A diode specifically designed to operate in reverse breakdown, maintaining a stable voltage across it, commonly used for voltage regulation, is called a
questions.explanation: Zener diodes are designed to operate safely in reverse breakdown, maintaining a stable output voltage, widely used in voltage regulator circuits.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A diode that emits visible (or invisible) light when forward biased is called a
questions.explanation: An LED emits light when forward biased, converting electrical energy into light energy, widely used as indicators and in displays.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A diode whose reverse current increases significantly when exposed to light, used in light-sensing applications, is called a
questions.explanation: A photodiode's reverse current is sensitive to light intensity, making it useful for light-sensing and detection applications.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The rectification process using only one diode (or one half of the input waveform) to convert AC to a pulsating DC output is called
questions.explanation: Half-wave rectification uses a single diode to conduct only during one half of the AC cycle, producing a pulsating output with significant gaps.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The rectification process that converts both halves of the AC input waveform into a smoother pulsating DC output is called
questions.explanation: Full-wave rectification utilises both halves of the AC cycle, producing a pulsating DC output with fewer gaps than half-wave rectification.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A full-wave rectifier design using a transformer with a centre-tapped secondary winding and two diodes is called a
questions.explanation: The centre-tapped design uses a transformer's centre tap along with two diodes to achieve full-wave rectification.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A full-wave rectifier design using four diodes arranged in a diamond configuration, without requiring a centre-tapped transformer, is called a
questions.explanation: The bridge rectifier uses four diodes arranged to achieve full-wave rectification without needing a centre-tapped transformer.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A filter circuit using a single capacitor connected across the rectifier's output to smooth the pulsating DC is called a
questions.explanation: A capacitor input filter smooths the rectifier's pulsating output by charging during peaks and discharging during troughs, reducing ripple.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A filter circuit using both an inductor and a capacitor together to more effectively smooth a rectifier's output is called an
questions.explanation: An LC filter combines an inductor (choke) and a capacitor to more effectively smooth the pulsating rectified output, further reducing ripple.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The measure of the remaining AC variation present in a filtered DC output is called the
questions.explanation: The ripple factor quantifies the amount of residual AC variation remaining in a supposedly smooth DC output after filtering.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A voltage regulation circuit using a Zener diode connected in parallel with the load to maintain a stable output voltage is called a
questions.explanation: A Zener shunt regulator places the Zener diode in parallel with the load, maintaining a stable voltage across it despite variations in supply or load current.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A bipolar junction transistor formed with a layer of P-type material sandwiched between two layers of N-type material is called an
questions.explanation: An NPN transistor has a thin P-type base region sandwiched between N-type emitter and collector regions.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A bipolar junction transistor formed with a layer of N-type material sandwiched between two layers of P-type material is called a
questions.explanation: A PNP transistor has a thin N-type base region sandwiched between P-type emitter and collector regions.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The operating mode of a transistor in which both junctions are reverse biased, and the transistor conducts essentially no current, is called the
questions.explanation: In cut-off, both transistor junctions are reverse biased, and the transistor behaves like an open switch, conducting almost no current.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The operating mode of a transistor in which the emitter-base junction is forward biased and the collector-base junction is reverse biased, allowing proportional amplification, is called the
questions.explanation: In the active region, a transistor amplifies current proportionally, making it the operating mode used for linear amplification.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The operating mode of a transistor in which both junctions are forward biased, and the transistor conducts maximum current, behaving like a closed switch, is called the
questions.explanation: In saturation, both junctions are forward biased, and the transistor conducts maximum current, effectively acting as a closed switch.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A transistor configuration in which the base terminal is common to both the input and output circuits is called the
questions.explanation: In the Common Base configuration, the base terminal is shared between input and output circuits, offering high voltage gain but low current gain.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A transistor configuration in which the emitter terminal is common to both the input and output circuits, and is the most widely used configuration for amplification, is called the
questions.explanation: The Common Emitter configuration, with the emitter shared between input and output, is the most commonly used transistor amplifier configuration.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A transistor configuration in which the collector terminal is common to both the input and output circuits, often used as a buffer with high current gain, is called the
questions.explanation: The Common Collector configuration (emitter follower) shares the collector terminal between input and output, offering high current gain and low output impedance, useful as a buffer.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The transistor current gain term 'alpha' (alpha) represents the ratio of
questions.explanation: Alpha (a common-base current gain) represents the ratio of collector current to emitter current, always slightly less than one.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The transistor current gain term 'beta' (beta) represents the ratio of
questions.explanation: Beta (a common-emitter current gain) represents the ratio of collector current to base current, and is related to alpha through the formula beta = alpha/(1-alpha).

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: When a transistor is used as an electronic switch, it typically operates between the
options: active region only, avoiding both extremes
questions.explanation: As a switch, a transistor is driven between cut-off (fully off) and saturation (fully on), rather than operating in its linear active region.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A key characteristic of a Zener diode used in a voltage regulator circuit is its
options: very high forward voltage drop compared to ordinary diodes
requirement to always be forward biased for regulation to occur
inability to conduct in either direction
stable, nearly constant reverse breakdown voltage over a range of currents
questions.explanation: Zener diodes maintain a relatively constant voltage across their terminals once in reverse breakdown, making them ideal for voltage regulation over a range of currents.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The forward voltage drop across a typical silicon signal diode, once conducting, is approximately
questions.explanation: A typical silicon diode has an approximate forward voltage drop of 0.7 volts once it begins conducting significantly.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The forward voltage drop across a typical germanium diode, once conducting, is approximately
questions.explanation: Germanium diodes typically have a lower forward voltage drop, around 0.3 volts, compared to silicon diodes at approximately 0.7 volts.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A key advantage of full-wave rectification over half-wave rectification is that it
options: produces a smoother output with less ripple, using both halves of the AC cycle
uses fewer diodes in every configuration
cannot be used with a bridge configuration at all
eliminates the need for any filtering capacitor
questions.explanation: By utilising both halves of the AC waveform, full-wave rectification produces a smoother, more consistent output with reduced ripple compared to half-wave rectification.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: An important precaution when installing an electrolytic capacitor in a circuit is to
options: always connect it in reverse to the marked polarity
avoid using it in any DC circuit
ignore polarity markings entirely, since they never matter
observe the correct polarity, as reversing it can cause the capacitor to fail or explode
questions.explanation: Electrolytic capacitors are polarised and can fail dramatically (including venting or exploding) if connected with reversed polarity.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: In a transistor amplifier, the emitter, base, and collector terminals are analogous in function to which parts of a water tap system controlling flow?
options: all three terminals perform an identical function with no distinction
only the emitter terminal has any functional role
the base acts like a small control valve, while the collector-emitter path carries the larger controlled flow
only the collector terminal has any functional role
questions.explanation: A helpful analogy: a small current at the base terminal controls a much larger current flowing through the collector-emitter path, similar to a valve controlling a larger flow.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A key parameter to consider when selecting a rectifier diode for a power supply is its
options: operating frequency in radio circuits only
maximum reverse voltage rating and maximum forward current rating
questions.explanation: Rectifier diode selection depends on ensuring the diode's maximum reverse voltage and forward current ratings safely exceed the circuit's actual operating conditions.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: Reverse breakdown in an ordinary (non-Zener) diode, if it occurs, generally
options: has no effect on the diode's performance
is a normal, safe, and desired mode of operation
risks permanently damaging the diode, unlike the controlled breakdown of a Zener diode
only occurs when the diode is forward biased
questions.explanation: Unlike Zener diodes, which are specifically designed to safely operate in reverse breakdown, ordinary diodes can be permanently damaged if driven into reverse breakdown.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: LEDs require a current-limiting resistor in most circuits mainly to
options: increase the LED's brightness far beyond its rated maximum
prevent excessive current from damaging the LED
convert AC current into DC current
reverse the polarity of the LED automatically
questions.explanation: A current-limiting resistor protects an LED from drawing excessive current, which could otherwise quickly damage or destroy it.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A single-stage transistor amplifier using the Common Emitter configuration is widely used mainly because it provides
options: both current and voltage gain, making it suitable for general-purpose amplification
current gain only, with no voltage gain
no gain of any kind, used purely for buffering
voltage gain only, with no current gain
questions.explanation: The Common Emitter amplifier configuration is popular because it provides significant gain in both current and voltage, unlike the other two configurations.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: In a transistor amplifier circuit, the network of resistors used to establish the correct DC operating point before an AC signal is applied is called the
questions.explanation: A biasing network sets up the correct DC voltages and currents needed for the transistor to operate correctly in its active region before amplifying an AC signal.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A capacitor used to connect the AC signal between amplifier stages while blocking DC voltage from passing through is called a
questions.explanation: A coupling capacitor allows AC signals to pass between stages while blocking the DC bias voltages of each stage from interfering with one another.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A capacitor placed across an emitter resistor to prevent AC signal loss (gain reduction) due to that resistor is called a
questions.explanation: A bypass capacitor provides a low-impedance AC path around the emitter resistor, preventing it from reducing the amplifier's overall AC gain.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A curve showing how an amplifier's gain varies across different signal frequencies is called its
questions.explanation: The frequency response curve illustrates how an amplifier's gain changes as the input signal frequency varies, important for assessing its suitability for different applications.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A circuit that generates a continuous, repetitive waveform, such as a sine wave, without an external AC input signal, is called an
questions.explanation: An oscillator generates its own repetitive output waveform, using feedback and amplification, without requiring an external AC input signal.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The condition that must be satisfied for a circuit to sustain continuous oscillation, involving the loop gain and phase shift, is called the
questions.explanation: The Barkhausen criterion states that sustained oscillation requires a loop gain of at least one and a total phase shift of zero (or a multiple of 360 degrees) around the feedback loop.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: An oscillator circuit that uses an inductor and capacitor together to determine its oscillation frequency is called an
questions.explanation: LC oscillators use the resonant properties of an inductor-capacitor combination (tank circuit) to establish and maintain their oscillation frequency.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The number system that uses ten digits (0 through 9) is called the
questions.explanation: The decimal system, used in everyday counting, is based on ten digits (0-9).

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The number system that uses only two digits (0 and 1), forming the fundamental basis of digital electronics, is called the
questions.explanation: The binary system uses only two digits (0 and 1), directly corresponding to the on/off states used within digital electronic circuits.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The number system that uses sixteen symbols (0-9 and A-F), often used as a compact way to represent binary values, is called the
questions.explanation: The hexadecimal system uses sixteen symbols, providing a more compact representation of binary data commonly used in computing and digital electronics.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The branch of mathematics dealing with logical operations on true/false (binary) values, foundational to digital logic design, is called
questions.explanation: Boolean algebra provides the mathematical framework for describing and simplifying logical operations, forming the basis of digital logic circuit design.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A logic gate that produces a true (1) output only when all of its inputs are true (1) is called an
questions.explanation: An AND gate outputs true only when every one of its inputs is true; otherwise its output is false.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A logic gate that produces a true (1) output when at least one of its inputs is true (1) is called an
questions.explanation: An OR gate outputs true if at least one of its inputs is true, and false only when all inputs are false.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A logic gate with a single input that inverts (reverses) the logical state of that input is called a
questions.explanation: A NOT gate (inverter) simply reverses its single input: a true input produces a false output, and vice versa.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A logic gate that produces the inverse output of an AND gate, being false only when all inputs are true, is called a
questions.explanation: A NAND gate is the logical inverse of an AND gate, producing a false output only when all its inputs are true.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A logic gate that produces the inverse output of an OR gate, being true only when all inputs are false, is called a
questions.explanation: A NOR gate is the logical inverse of an OR gate, producing a true output only when every input is false.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A logic gate that produces a true output only when its inputs are different from each other is called an
questions.explanation: An XOR gate outputs true only when its inputs differ (one true, one false), and false when the inputs are the same.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A logic gate that produces a true output only when its inputs are the same as each other is called an
questions.explanation: An XNOR gate is the inverse of an XOR gate, outputting true when its inputs match (both true or both false).

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: An instrument used to visually display and monitor how a voltage waveform changes over time is called a
questions.explanation: A CRO displays voltage waveforms visually on a screen, allowing engineers and technicians to observe how a signal changes over time.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A chemical substance applied during soldering to clean the metal surfaces and improve the flow and adhesion of solder is called
questions.explanation: Flux cleans oxidation from metal surfaces and improves the wetting and flow of solder, producing a stronger, more reliable joint.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A tool used to remove excess solder from a joint, often to correct mistakes or replace a faulty component, is called a
questions.explanation: A desoldering pump quickly draws away melted solder from a joint, allowing components to be removed or corrections made.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A flat board with conductive copper tracks, used to mechanically support and electrically connect electronic components, is called a
questions.explanation: A PCB provides both mechanical support and electrical connections for components, using etched copper tracks instead of loose wiring.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A systematic process of identifying and resolving faults on an electronic circuit board is generally called
questions.explanation: Troubleshooting involves methodically testing and inspecting a circuit board to identify and correct faults preventing correct operation.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The decimal number 5 is represented in binary as
questions.explanation: Decimal 5 equals binary 101, since 1x4 + 0x2 + 1x1 = 5.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The decimal number 10 is represented in binary as
questions.explanation: Decimal 10 equals binary 1010, since 1x8 + 0x4 + 1x2 + 0x1 = 10.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A table listing all possible input combinations of a logic circuit alongside their corresponding outputs is called a
questions.explanation: A truth table systematically lists every possible input combination for a logic circuit and the resulting output for each, essential for digital logic design.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The Boolean expression for an AND gate with inputs A and B is typically written as
questions.explanation: The AND operation is conventionally represented using a dot (or simple juxtaposition) between the input variables, such as A.B.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The Boolean expression for an OR gate with inputs A and B is typically written as
questions.explanation: The OR operation is conventionally represented using a plus sign between the input variables, such as A+B.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: The main function of a CRO's time base control is to
options: change the frequency of the signal being measured
adjust only the vertical amplitude of the displayed waveform
convert AC signals into DC signals
adjust the horizontal sweep speed, controlling how the waveform is displayed over time
questions.explanation: The time base control adjusts how quickly the CRO's electron beam sweeps horizontally, determining how the waveform is stretched or compressed over time on the display.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: Before soldering a joint, it is generally recommended to first ensure that the surfaces to be joined are
options: already coated with a thick layer of old solder
clean and free from dirt, oxidation, or grease
questions.explanation: Clean surfaces, free from dirt, oxidation, or grease, are essential for solder to properly wet and bond to the metal, forming a reliable joint.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.text: A cold solder joint, resulting from insufficient heat during soldering, typically appears
options: dull, grainy, and may be mechanically or electrically unreliable
identical in every way to a properly soldered joint
only a cosmetic issue with no effect on reliability
questions.explanation: A cold solder joint, caused by insufficient heating, typically looks dull and grainy rather than shiny and smooth, and can be mechanically weak or electrically intermittent.
